title: Close the month without the scramble
goal: You will reconcile the period, lock A/R and A/P, complete its close checklist, and mark the accounting period closed.
prerequisites: A/R, A/P, and bank activity entered through period end
Period-end bank statement and reconciliation balances
Approval to lock transactions and close the period

steps.action: Open the close checklist for the accounting period you intend to close.
steps.where: Setup > Accounting > Manage Accounting Periods, then the Checklist icon beside the target period.
steps.why: The checklist shows the period's status, dependencies, and unfinished closing tasks.
steps.checkpoint: The Accounting Period Close Checklist page shows the correct period name and a list of closing tasks.
hint_levels: Find the period in the accounting periods list.
Use the Checklist icon on the same row as the period you are closing.
Click Setup > Accounting > Manage Accounting Periods, locate the target period, then click its Checklist icon.

steps.action: Run the A/R Aging Summary as of the period-end date.
steps.where: Reports > Customer/Receivables > A/R Aging Summary, using the As Of date filter.
steps.why: The aging total must support the accounts receivable balance before A/R is locked.
steps.checkpoint: The report header shows the period-end As Of date and the Total column displays the receivables balance.
hint_levels: Start with the customer receivables reports.
Set the aging report's cutoff to the final day of the period.
Click Reports > Customer/Receivables > A/R Aging Summary, set As Of to the period-end date, then click Refresh.

steps.action: Run the A/P Aging Summary as of the period-end date.
steps.where: Reports > Vendors/Payables > A/P Aging Summary, using the As Of date filter.
steps.why: The aging total must support the accounts payable balance before A/P is locked.
steps.checkpoint: The report header shows the period-end As Of date and the Total column displays the payables balance.
hint_levels: Move to the vendor payables reports.
Use the A/P aging report with the same period-end cutoff.
Click Reports > Vendors/Payables > A/P Aging Summary, set As Of to the period-end date, then click Refresh.

steps.action: Reconcile each period-end bank or credit-card statement.
steps.where: Transactions > Bank > Reconcile Account Statement, in the Account and Statement Date fields and transaction-matching list.
steps.why: Reconciliation confirms that cash and card balances agree with external statements.
steps.checkpoint: The reconciliation shows a Difference of 0.00 and the statement is saved as reconciled.
hint_levels: Use the account reconciliation page and watch the Difference field.
Choose the account and statement date, match cleared transactions, and resolve any remaining difference.
Click Transactions > Bank > Reconcile Account Statement, select the account, enter the statement date and ending balance, mark matched transactions, confirm Difference is 0.00, then click Reconcile.

steps.action: Lock accounts receivable for the target period.
steps.where: Setup > Accounting > Manage Accounting Periods > target period Checklist > Lock A/R task.
steps.why: Locking A/R prevents new posting activity from changing the reconciled receivables balance.
steps.checkpoint: The Lock A/R checklist row displays a completed status or check mark.
hint_levels: Return to the period checklist and find the receivables lock.
Open Lock A/R, select the relevant subsidiaries if prompted, and submit the task.
Click Setup > Accounting > Manage Accounting Periods, click the period's Checklist icon, click Lock A/R, select subsidiaries if shown, then click Submit.

steps.action: Lock accounts payable for the target period.
steps.where: Target period's Accounting Period Close Checklist > Lock A/P task.
steps.why: Locking A/P prevents new vendor postings from changing the reconciled payables balance.
steps.checkpoint: The Lock A/P checklist row displays a completed status or check mark.
hint_levels: The payables lock is another task on the same checklist.
Open Lock A/P and apply it to the same subsidiary scope used for A/R.
On the Accounting Period Close Checklist, click Lock A/P, select subsidiaries if shown, then click Submit.

steps.action: Run the Trial Balance for the target period and confirm the debit and credit totals agree.
steps.where: Reports > Financial > Trial Balance, using the period and subsidiary filters.
steps.why: A balanced trial balance is the final control check before all posting is locked.
steps.checkpoint: The report shows the target period and equal debit and credit grand totals.
hint_levels: Use the main financial reports and verify both grand totals.
Filter Trial Balance to the closing period and the subsidiary scope being closed.
Click Reports > Financial > Trial Balance, set the Period and Subsidiary filters, click Refresh, then compare the debit and credit totals.

steps.action: Complete each remaining required task on the period's close checklist.
steps.where: Setup > Accounting > Manage Accounting Periods > target period Checklist, in each incomplete task row.
steps.why: NetSuite will not allow the final close while prerequisite checklist tasks remain unfinished.
steps.checkpoint: Every required row above Close Period displays a completed status or check mark.
hint_levels: Look for checklist rows without completed marks.
Open incomplete tasks in order because later tasks may depend on earlier ones.
Return to the target period's Checklist and open each incomplete row from top to bottom, complete its displayed form, and click Submit until only Close Period remains.

steps.action: Lock all remaining posting activity for the period.
steps.where: Target period's Accounting Period Close Checklist > Lock All task.
steps.why: This freezes general-ledger posting after reconciliations and adjustments are complete.
steps.checkpoint: The Lock All checklist row displays a completed status or check mark.
hint_levels: Use the final locking task before the close action.
Confirm the subsidiary scope, then complete Lock All.
On the period checklist, click Lock All, select the applicable subsidiaries if shown, then click Submit.

steps.where: Target period's Accounting Period Close Checklist > Close Period task.
steps.why: Closing the period records completion and blocks ordinary posting into it.
steps.checkpoint: The checklist shows Close Period as completed and Manage Accounting Periods shows the period as closed.
hint_levels: The final action is at the bottom of the completed checklist.
Open Close Period only after every prerequisite row is complete.
On the Accounting Period Close Checklist, click Close Period, confirm the period and subsidiary scope, then click Submit.
